candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / De Incarnatione Verbi §22
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi (On the Incarnation), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 25 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria De Incarnatione Verbi §22 (c. 350 AD)

'For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption' (LXX 15:10 — ouk enkataleipseis tēn psychēn mou eis hadēn, oude dōseis ton hosion sou idein diaphthoran) — Athanasius marks Ps 16:10 as the DEFINITIVE RESURRECTION-PROOFTEXT, citing Peter's exposition (Acts 2:25-31) and Paul's (Acts 13:35-37) as canonical-apostolic exegesis: the verse cannot be of David (whose tomb remains) but must be of David's-greater-Son, the Word-incarnate, whose flesh in the tomb did-not-see-corruption (idein diaphthoran) because the deathless-Word remained-united-to-it even through the three-day-pause. The non-corruption of the dead-flesh-of-Christ is the soteriological-key: by-Word's-presence-in-it, death itself is decomposed-from-within. Tewahedo Holy-Saturday liturgy cites Ps 16:10 + Acts 2:27 as the harrowing-of-Hades-anchor-pair.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Athanasius of Alexandria, De Incarnatione Verbi §22. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.
